This long trailer needs patient steering; watch cab front-left clearance as well as the rear. Near the bay, the end rail distorts corridor estimates and provokes sharp steering. Prioritise painted bay alignment there; hitch angle alone does not tell whether the trailer is aligned with the bay.

notes_in.text: Look at the camera screen at minus 23 degrees. The course bends right, then straightens. Tracking the rail midpoint about 4 metres behind the trailer at 0.65 m/s worked without contact or forward pulls. When all bay corners appear, remember their centreline and heading, then follow that alignment at 0.45 m/s as corners disappear. Stop using rail midpoints near the dock: the end wall distorts them. Straighten early. This short trailer needs prompt follow steering towards the hitch swing to prevent folding.

Left-mirror following alone failed in the first bend: the trailer rear crowded the left rail while left steering in reverse swung the tractor front into the right rail. Repeated short pull-ups alternated those contacts without fixing the offset. Check both rails early and leave room for the tractor's front swing; do not trust a fixed offset from one rail. This short trailer reacts quickly: shape the approach early and follow its swing gently. Earlier drivers also struggled at the second pinch; reset before entering and use painted bay corners for final alignment.

A shallow right bend clears the opening. Near the bay, a late or gentle right curve repeatedly caught the cart rear-left. Pull well clear and start a firmer right curve earlier, then straighten before the narrow opening; this cleared it. Straight reversing then caught the rear-right near the finish. Back out and begin a gentle left correction before that corner, then straighten into the bay. Prioritise cart rear-corner clearance over chasing paint. This short cart needs constant hitch correction even at a crawl; pull forward to recover before it folds.
